Welford and Wickham C.E. (V.A.) Primary School
"This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you." John 15:12
Welcome to our wonderful school
Welford and Wickham C.E. (V.A.) Primary School is a small, rural, Church of England primary school, situated between Newbury and Hungerford, for children aged 4-11 years. There is capacity for 105 children on roll, enabling all staff to know individual children and their families well and provide a nurturing and supportive school environment. The school provides a warm and happy atmosphere and an exciting, stimulating learning environment.
Welford and Wickham C.E. (V.A.) Primary School benefits from being part of the Kite Primary Federation, working closely with Stockcross C.E. (V.A.) Primary School to provide the very best opportunities for the children whilst maintaining the unique character of this special, small school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chair of Governor’s Welcome - Welford and Wickham C.E. (V.A.) Primary School
pageCache.text:
Chair of Governor’s Welcome
Chair of Governor’s Welcome
As Chair of Governors I am delighted to be part of the Wickham and Welford school community and The Kite Primary Federation.
The role of a governing board is to work alongside and support the Executive Head Teacher, Mrs Lagares, so that she and her staff can fulfil their roles in all aspects of teaching and learning.
As governors we come from a wide range of backgrounds with skills in the field of education, marketing, finance, entrepreneurship, business and well-being.
We are all volunteers who come together to use these skills to promote the ongoing development and improvement of all areas of school life.
As part of the Kite Federation, alongside our sister school at Stockcross, our vision is that:
“ We are all respectful, loving and responsible individuals who will try our best together through challenge and perseverance.”
This is underpinned by the school’s four strong Christian values of Love, Respect, Perseverance and Challenge.
If you are a prospective parent reading this, we would be delighted to welcome you to join and become part of our wonderful village school.
I encourage you to make an appointment with the office and come to see our very special school for yourself.
The Kite Primary Federation

Croc After School Club
Collecting your child from Crocodile Club
When you are collecting your child please go to the school door and ring our doorbell. Our doorbell is a motion detector video recorder (CCTV) and will alert us of your presence.
YOU MUST NOT ENTER THE SCHOOL BUILDING. A STAFF MEMBER WILL BRING YOUR CHILD TO YOU.
Contact details
Mobile numbers must only be used for Crocodile Club only. If you wish to discuss a school matter please contact the school office.
Crocinfo@stockcross.org.uk
(payment and booking queries)
Crocfinance@stockcross.org.uk
Paula Allen (EYFS Key Person)
Crocinfo@stockcross.org.uk
Croc After School Club
Children from Welford and Wickham school can access wraparound childcare from the Crocodile Club based at Stockcross school. Children are transported to Stockcross via the school minibus and children are collected from there.
Crocodile Club is an after-school childcare provision which runs from 3.15pm to 5.45pm from Monday to Thursdays in term-time. The club is staffed by three experienced learning support assistants and the KPF Federation School Business Manager. It is based at Stockcross school and runs on the school site. Crocodile Club is run separately to the school, so after initial contact has been made, the school office will pass you to the Club Manager to answer any queries you may have. The emphasis is on outdoor fun, when the weather permits, and we move into the school hall for activities. The play is led by the children following the play work principles encouraging independence and resilience. Each EYFS child will have a Key Person assigned to them, to aid in a smooth induction please fill the “all about me” form too.
Each session costs £13.75 per child, payable either by BACS or childcare vouchers and sessions are booked on a termly basis. The welcome pack below includes all booking forms and should be completed and returned to the school so that your child’s place can be confirmed. Please take a look at our handbook as that may answer more questions you have.
Once your child is registered you will be invited to join the croc “class dojo” page where you can see what the children have been experiencing at Croc Club

pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club
The Kite Primary Federation runs a flexible Breakfast Club, at Welford and Wickham School, which is open to all pupils from the Federation. Children will enjoy a healthy breakfast (cereal, toast etc.) with their friends in a safe and nurturing environment.
It opens its doors at 8am and Welford and Wickham children are taken to their classrooms ready for the start of the school day. Children from Stockcross are transported to school, via the school minibus, which arrives at school before the start of the school day.
Bookings can be made online up to the day before, allowing a truly flexible childcare provision. For further information please contact the Welford school office office@welford.w-berks.sch.uk . Payment is taken upon booking confirmation and childcare vouchers and tax-free childcare is accepted. Sessions are charged at £5 per session, which includes breakfast.
The form below will need to be completed for children attending from Stockcross, for the first time.

Welcome to Balmoral Class
At Welford & Wickham, Years Reception, 1 & 2 are taught together as Balmoral class. Miss Kammeyer is class teacher. Mrs Barrett is also there to help us everyday too.

Every day the reception children will have the opportunity for independent learning where they plan their own time and use their interests to explore and apply the skills that they have learnt.

Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
SEND
All pupils at Welford and Wickham have the right to access broad, balanced and challenging learning opportunities and as such all pupils are included in all aspects of school life. At some point during their time at Welford and Wickham any child could have a special educational need whether it is temporary or more permanent. The term Special Educational Need refers to a wide range of learning, social and emotional or physical difficulties that may have an impact on the child’s learning ability or ability to access the curriculum.
We keep a Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) register of children who need support which is ‘additional to and different from’ the majority of pupils in school. Each child on the SEND register has a Success and Achievement Plan (SAP) with personalised targets.
At the heart of the SEN Code of Practice (2014), is the importance of maintaining a person-centred approach to supporting children on the SEND register. This is an ethos which we whole heartedly support and we encourage parents, and their children, to play an active role in personalised target setting and sharing their aspirations when writing and reviewing a SAP. We strive to keep parents as fully informed as possible and aim to work in partnership with our families.
Our SENDCo is Mrs Sutherland.

Online Safety
Useful Links
At school, we teach children about e-safety issues and appropriate behaviours, helping them to develop the skills to keep themselves safe online. We are aware that some children have access to YouTube and social media at home, exposing them to images and risk that they may find difficult to cope with. We therefore wish to foster a collaborative approach to e-safety, with the involvement of parents and carers, by sharing strategies to keep children safe online, and hope that the links provided here will help increase awareness of risks, and provide guidance for discussion at home.

School Day
In a typical week, there are 32.5 hours. Morning registration is at 8.45am when the school day begins.
The school operates a ‘kiss and drop’ facility, to enable parents to drop their child off safely without needing to park. The doors open and Kiss and Drop begins at 8.35am until school starts at 8.45am.
